facts.statement: One base player body diameter is the spatial normalization unit.
facts.method: Defines the project unit and anchors all footage normalization.

facts.statement: Base maximum health is normalized to one.
facts.method: Defines the health unit used by proportional card and damage values.

facts.statement: The damage and environment collider is approximately circular, while arms, gun, face, and hat are presentation.

tolerance.value: stable rolling contact and radial hits

facts.method: Compared rotating body silhouettes, ledge contacts, and projectile impacts.

facts.statement: Base sustained horizontal speed is about 0.10 player diameters per simulation tick.
facts.method: Normalized one collision-free 33-frame floor run; a second early-match trajectory is retained but excluded because its overlapping shot prevents recoil from being separated.

facts.statement: Ground control reaches sustained speed in roughly eight ticks.
facts.method: Provisional tuning hypothesis derived by dividing the sustained-speed target by an eight-tick response target; the selected footage does not isolate the full acceleration ramp.

facts.statement: Airborne horizontal control retains most ground authority.
facts.method: Provisional tuning hypothesis constrained by visible airborne corrections; the selected footage does not isolate equal-duration ground and air input.

facts.statement: A player stores one jump that may be used on the ground or in the air and is restored by ground contact.
facts.method: Cross-checked the moveset description with ledge-fall and grounded-jump sequences.

facts.statement: A base jump begins near 0.25 player diameters per tick upward.
facts.method: Algebraic implementation hypothesis derived from the measured jump-height and time-to-apex bands rather than a direct frame-to-frame launch-velocity observation.

facts.statement: Base airborne gravity is near 0.007 player diameters per tick squared.
facts.method: Algebraic implementation hypothesis derived from the measured jump-height and time-to-apex bands rather than a direct acceleration observation.

facts.statement: A base jump rises roughly 4.5 player diameters above takeoff.
facts.method: Normalized one collision-free visible rise against body diameter; a second arc is retained but excluded because it contains a shot.

facts.statement: A base jump reaches its apex in about 36 ticks.
facts.method: Counted one collision-free 30 fps rise interval and converted each frame to approximately two simulation ticks; a shot-contaminated comparison is excluded.

facts.statement: Releasing horizontal input damps ground velocity quickly without an immediate hard stop.
facts.method: Provisional tuning hypothesis constrained by short settling motions; the selected footage does not expose a clean input-release timestamp.

facts.statement: The circular body rotates visibly from contacts, recoil, and knockback while aim remains world-directed.

tolerance.value: body rotation does not rotate aim input

facts.method: Observed independent body roll and gun aiming in both recordings.

facts.statement: Base players do not regenerate health during a duel.
facts.method: Observed persistent damage between hits where no healing card was present.
